newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to issue long-term fx-linked bonds by end-97-min.
newsitem.headline: Greece to issue long-term fx-linked bonds by end-97-min.

text.p: Greece will issue long-term foreign currency-linked bonds by year-end to make yield spread comparisons with drachma-denominated bonds possible, Deputy Finance Minister Nicos Christodoulakis told reporters.
"We will issue forex-linked bonds by end-97," said Christodoulakis. ".. it will make it possible to compare yield spreads with long-term drachma bonds."
The ministry has not decided yet what type of foreign currency will be used, he said.

Asked whether yield comparisons could be made by using outstanding foreign currency-denominated Eurobonds of the Hellenic Republic, the minister said bonds should be of the same maturity to make meaningful comparisons.
"This is what benchmarking is all about," said Christodoulakis.
Greece will auction 150 billion drachmas of three-year fixed coupon bonds, 100 billion of five-year coupon bonds and 50 billion of seven-year coupon bonds on March 19.
It is the first time ever that Greece auctions five- and seven-year fixed coupon drachma bonds.
The deputy finance minister declined to specify the coupons on the fixed-coupon debt instruments to be auctioned on March 19.

Asked whether the likely foreign exchange risk inherent in the seven-year coupon bonds if the drachma was converted into euros during the lifetime of the instrument made it less attractive, the minister answered "no".
"What is important is the timing (of conversion)," said Christodoulakis. "These bonds should be very attractive because inflation under euro would be much lower than current inflation."
Greek CPI inflation eased to 6.6 percent year-on-year in February from 6.8 percent in January.
The euro/drachma conversion rate was not an important issue because there would be no national EU currencies at the time of converting drachmas into euros, he added.
Christodoulakis said the market reception for government bonds auctioned by other "Club Med" countries facing similar dilemmas had been very warm and expected a similar reception for the Greek bonds.
The deputy finance minister said the Greek inflation-linked bonds to be issued or auctioned in April would be long-term and carry coupons. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
